flashcards.q: When should you use adjacency list vs adjacency matrix?
flashcards.a: Adjacency list (O(V+E) space) for sparse graphs -- almost always. Adjacency matrix (O(V^2) space, O(1) edge check) only for dense graphs or naturally matrix-shaped algorithms like Floyd-Warshall.

flashcards.q: Why is undirected cycle detection different from directed cycle detection?
flashcards.a: Undirected needs only visited/unvisited plus parent-exclusion (every edge is stored both ways, so you must not count walking back to your parent as a cycle). Directed needs three-color state (white/gray/black) because an edge to an already-fully-processed node can be a valid DAG convergence, not a cycle -- only an edge to a GRAY (active ancestor) node is a real cycle.

flashcards.q: What is the BFS layer invariant and why does it guarantee shortest path in an unweighted graph?
flashcards.a: Everything at distance d is fully processed before anything at distance d+1 is discovered, enforced by the FIFO queue -- so the first time you reach a node is guaranteed to be via the shortest (fewest-edge) path.

flashcards.q: What is the exact theorem connecting bipartiteness to cycles?
flashcards.a: A graph is bipartite if and only if it contains no odd-length cycle -- the 2-coloring attempt during BFS/DFS is a complete decision procedure for this, not a heuristic.

flashcards.q: What is a back edge in DFS and what does it signify?
flashcards.a: An edge to a GRAY node (currently on the active recursion stack / an ancestor in the current DFS path) -- the unique signature of a cycle in a directed graph.

flashcards.q: Why can undirected graphs never have cross edges in DFS classification, only tree/back edges?
flashcards.a: By the time DFS finishes exploring a subtree in an undirected graph, every edge leaving that subtree has already been examined (edges are bidirectional), so any non-tree edge must have already been classified as a back edge from that subtree's perspective.

flashcards.q: What is 0-1 BFS and why is it faster than Dijkstra for graphs with only weight-0 and weight-1 edges?
flashcards.a: Use a deque: push 0-weight edges to the front, 1-weight edges to the back, maintaining sorted-distance order without a heap. O(V+E) vs Dijkstra's O((V+E) log V).

flashcards.q: What's the most common bug when building a directed graph's adjacency list, and what does it break?
flashcards.a: Adding the edge both ways (copy-pasting undirected construction code) -- silently turns the DAG into a graph with trivial 2-cycles everywhere, breaking topological sort and directed cycle detection.
